title: Dedicated capacity onramp: approval lifecycle, throughput SLAs, and autoscale safeguards
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Define and deliver a repeatable onramp workflow for customers requesting Dedicated capacity that ties reservation intake, approval gating, throughput guarantees, and autoscaling policy templates into a single operational flow. The goal is to reduce time-to-first-reservation from sales handoff to live capacity, ensure SLAs map to autoscale and fallback policies, and provide a clear audit trail for finance and security reviews.

Scope: 1) Intake form and enrichment rules for capacity requests (expected throughput, peak QPS, sequence lengths, model families). 2) Approval matrix (finance, security, infra) and automated gating in the console. 3) Mapping table that converts requested throughput into GPU pool sizing and expected cost estimate. 4) Autoscale policy templates (min/max pools, burst allowances, cooldown windows) and associated safety limits to protect shared fleet. 5) SLA/throughput guarantee language and corresponding runtime circuit-breaker/fallback behavior. 6) Ops runbook for oncall handoff and emergency scale-out.

Acceptance criteria: - Intake form stored in CRM + Console, with automated validations for incompatible region/model combos. - Approval gates implemented in the reservation workflow with email/Slack notifications and an auditable approval log. - Autoscale policy templates present in the console and applied automatically at provisioning with sensible defaults (min capacity, burst buffer, cooldown). - A deterministic sizing algorithm and cost estimator that annotates reservations with expected hourly spend and a sensitivity band (+/- 20%). - SLAs for throughput expressed as p95 throughput and mean active GPU utilization; runtime fallback to lower-cost model variant and cross-region routing defined and tested. - Security and finance signoff captured; security checklist enforced before private deployments.

Constraints and assumptions: - We must reuse existing billing and quota primitives in the Console. - For early customers, manual approvals may be required; automation should be opt-in per customer. - Sizing model initially targets common model families (Llama/Redwood variants) and 32/80GB GPU types. - Autoscale will not provision new hardware instantly — burst is limited to reserved burst pools and regional capacity pools.

Metrics to monitor: - Time from reservation creation to capacity live (target: < 3 business days for standard requests). - Reservation approval cycle time. - Incidence of SLA breaches on dedicated pools (target: 99.9% availability for committed throughput). - Cost estimation variance vs actual spend.

Stakeholders: Sales Solutions, Finance, Security, Runtime Eng, Capacity Ops, Customer Success.
